title: LIVAK: A High-Performance In-Memory Learned Index for Variable-Length Keys
problem: Existing learned indexes are inefficient when handling variable-length keys, creating a structural mismatch between learned index assumptions and real-world variable-length key requirements. Supporting variable-length keys efficiently in learned indexes requires novel architectural approaches.
motivation: Learned indexes have proven efficient for in-memory data access, and enabling them to handle variable-length keys would significantly expand their applicability to real-world database workloads.
method: LIVAK uses a hybrid structure combining trie, learned index, and B+-tree components where each node indexes an 8-byte key slice. Learned indexes are selectively used for large nodes where they provide performance benefits, while B+-trees handle small nodes. A character re-encoding mechanism prevents performance degradation across variable-length inputs.
key_novelty: A hybrid indexing architecture that strategically applies learned indexes only to large nodes while using B+-trees for small nodes, with character re-encoding to efficiently support variable-length keys.
contributions: LIVAK: a hybrid learned index structure combining trie, learned index, and B+-tree for variable-length keys
Character re-encoding mechanism to prevent performance degradation
Comprehensive empirical evaluation against B+-tree, Masstree, and SIndex
Adaptive node-level index selection strategy for efficiency
primary_theme: hybrid learned indexing for variable-length database keys
